newsitem.title: JAPAN: SHIN-ETSU CHEM SAYS EXPLOSION SHUTS SILANE PLANT.
newsitem.headline: SHIN-ETSU CHEM SAYS EXPLOSION SHUTS SILANE PLANT.

text.p: Shin-Etsu Chemical Co Ltd said on Wednesday that a blast on Tuesday night hit a silicone production facility in central Japan, halting output of certain types of silane, a form of silicone.
The blast, which occurred late on Tuesday evening, injured one worker, the company said in a statement.
Other facilities at the plant, located in Naoetsu, Niigata Prefecture, are operating normally, it said.
A company spokesman had no immediate comment on the possible impact of the blast on the company's silicone business.
He added that the cause of the explosion had not yet been identified and that the company did not know when the silane facility would be able to resume operations.
"We are now reviewing our future supply situation for silane," the Shin-Etsu statement said.
The spokesman declined to comment on the volume of production in recent months at the Naoetsu facility or on its production capacity.
Shin-Etsu also has another, larger silicone plant in Gunma prefecture, near Tokyo, the spokesman said.

Kyodo news agency quoted a police spokesman as saying a one-metre diameter cylinder used for making test chemicals in the silicone production process exploded, injuring a 40-year-old worker who suffered severe burns.
It quoted the spokesman as saying there was no fire but the blast damaged four nearby homes.
